readingA.passage:
Water covers most of our planet, yet only a tiny part of it is fresh water that we can drink. Rivers, lakes and underground water are shared by people, animals and plants. In many Indian towns, women and children still walk long distances every morning to fetch a few pots of water. During summer the wells dry up and tankers become the only hope.
Much of this shortage is caused by our own carelessness. Taps are left running, pipes leak for weeks and rainwater simply flows away into drains. Factories pour waste into rivers and make the water unfit for use. Farmers often grow crops that need a great deal of water even in dry regions.
The good news is that simple steps can make a big difference. Rainwater harvesting allows us to collect the rain from rooftops and send it back into the ground. Repairing leaks, closing taps while brushing and reusing the water used for washing vegetables to water plants can save hundreds of litres every week. If every family saves a little, the whole community will have enough.

readingB.passage:
Every year thousands of migratory birds travel to India from cold countries such as Siberia and Central Asia. When winter covers their homes with ice and snow, food becomes scarce, so they fly thousands of kilometres to warmer lands. Wetlands like Bharatpur in Rajasthan and Chilika Lake in Odisha become lively with flamingos, cranes, ducks and pelicans.
Scientists are still amazed at how these birds find their way. They seem to use the position of the sun and stars, the earth's magnetic field and familiar landmarks such as rivers and mountains. Many of them fly in a V-shape, which saves energy because each bird is helped by the air moving off the wings of the bird ahead.
Sadly, these visitors face many dangers. Wetlands are being drained for buildings and farms, lakes are polluted, and some birds are hunted illegally. Power lines and tall towers also cause deaths. Protecting wetlands and creating awareness among local people can ensure that our winged guests keep returning every year.
words: Find words from the passage that mean: (a) not enough (b) surprised
qa: Why do migratory birds come to India every year?
Winter covers their homes in cold countries like Siberia with ice and snow and food becomes scarce, so they fly to warmer lands like India.
How do migratory birds find their way?
They seem to use the position of the sun and stars, the earth's magnetic field and landmarks such as rivers and mountains.
What dangers do migratory birds face?
Wetlands are drained for buildings and farms, lakes are polluted, some birds are hunted illegally, and power lines and towers cause deaths.

readingA.passage:
Mahatma Gandhi believed that the real India lives in its villages. He dreamt of villages that were clean, self-reliant and full of cottage industries. He encouraged people to spin khadi on the charkha so that every home could earn some money and depend less on foreign goods.
Gandhiji also stressed cleanliness. He himself cleaned toilets in his ashram and taught others that no work is low or dirty. He felt that a clean village would also be a healthy village, free from many diseases.
Education was another of his concerns. His idea of 'basic education' meant that children should learn through useful crafts like weaving, gardening and carpentry, and should also learn to respect manual labour. He believed that education must build character, not just fill the mind with facts.
Today many of these ideas are coming back in new forms. Campaigns for cleanliness, skill training and support for local products show that Gandhiji's vision of a self-reliant India is still alive.

readingB.passage:
Yoga is an ancient Indian practice that joins the body, mind and breath. The word 'yoga' comes from the Sanskrit word 'yuj', which means 'to unite'. Today people all over the world practise it, and since 2015 the United Nations has celebrated 21 June as International Day of Yoga.
Regular yoga makes the body flexible and strong. Asanas, or postures, stretch the muscles and improve balance. Pranayama, or breathing exercises, increases the supply of oxygen and calms the nerves. Meditation helps people concentrate and reduces stress, anger and anxiety.
Doctors say that yoga can help people with problems like back pain, high blood pressure and sleeplessness. Students who practise yoga often find that they remember lessons better and feel less nervous before examinations.
However, yoga should be learnt from a trained teacher. Some postures can cause injury if done wrongly or too quickly. Yoga is best done on an empty stomach, in fresh air, and with patience, because its benefits grow slowly over time.
words: Find words from the passage opposite in meaning to: (a) stiff (b) excites
qa: What is the meaning of 'yoga' and where does the word come from?
The word comes from the Sanskrit word 'yuj', which means 'to unite'; yoga unites the body, mind and breath.
It helps them remember lessons better, concentrate, and feel less nervous and stressed before examinations.
What precautions should be taken while doing yoga?
It should be learnt from a trained teacher, postures should not be done wrongly or too fast, and it should be done on an empty stomach in fresh air, with patience.

readingA.passage:
Kalpana Chawla was born in Karnal, Haryana, in 1962. As a little girl she loved to watch aeroplanes flying over her town and often drew pictures of them. Her teachers remembered her as a curious student who asked many questions.
After studying aeronautical engineering in Chandigarh, she went to the United States for higher studies and earned a doctorate. In 1994 she was selected by NASA as an astronaut. In 1997 she became the first woman of Indian origin to go into space, travelling more than ten million kilometres around the earth.
In 2003 she flew on her second mission aboard the space shuttle Columbia. Sadly, on its return journey the shuttle broke apart just minutes before landing, and all seven crew members lost their lives.
Kalpana's life continues to inspire young people, especially girls from small towns. She showed that with hard work, courage and a big dream, nothing is impossible. Schools, hostels and even a satellite have been named after her.

readingB.passage:
Honey bees are among the most useful insects on earth. A single colony can have up to fifty thousand bees, and every bee has a job. The queen lays eggs, the drones mate with the queen, and the worker bees — all female — collect nectar, make honey, clean the hive and guard it.
Bees are famous for honey, but their greatest service is pollination. As a bee moves from flower to flower, pollen sticks to its body and is carried to other flowers, helping plants form fruits and seeds. About one-third of the food we eat, including apples, almonds and many vegetables, depends on pollinators like bees.
Unfortunately bee populations are falling in many countries. The heavy use of pesticides, the loss of wild flowers, pollution and changes in climate are the main causes. Without bees, farmers would harvest much less, and food would become costly.
We can help by growing flowering plants, avoiding harmful chemicals in our gardens and buying honey from local beekeepers.
words: Find words from the passage that mean: (a) protect (b) expensive
qa: What are the duties of the worker bees?
The worker bees, all female, collect nectar, make honey, clean the hive and guard it.
Why is pollination called the bees' greatest service?
Bees carry pollen from flower to flower, helping plants form fruits and seeds; about one-third of our food depends on pollinators like bees.
Why are bee populations falling and how can we help?
Heavy use of pesticides, loss of wild flowers, pollution and climate change. We can grow flowering plants, avoid harmful chemicals and buy honey from local beekeepers.
